CodeElement: Authoritative 3D material and geometry edits
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Outside solid is Void. Immutable rock takes precedence. Newest covering edit determines Void for excavation or Soil for fill. Otherwise seed voids then soil.
InformationChannel: Ordered half-open cuboids, precedence and material-volume authority
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for solid representation.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Physical state and material conservation support reproducible experiments.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Box precedence and exact ledgers specify representation. They cannot stand in for architecture, material mechanics or ant cognition.

CodeElement: Physical clearance, geometry query and portal distinction
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Continuous clearance checks surface intersections and a swept physical box against solid cells. Legacy geometry requires quantized endpoints and a conservative swept bounding box. Food or soil custody selects larger body half extent.
InformationChannel: Physical sweeps, box clearance, exact graph and administrative route access
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for sweep or host route.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The solver tests modeled clearance and topology.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: World A* and portal metadata are host diagnostics, not an ant perception channel. Static load clearance is a coarse body model.

CodeElement: Local excavation candidate and soil work
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Require work duration, local reach, no rock and positive excavatable volume. Reject loaded or over-capacity worker and inadequate loaded clearance. If physiology is enabled require energy strictly above cost.
InformationChannel: Geometry lookup, face accessibility, capacity, energy and timed proposal
EvidenceLocators: B3-N01 pp. 434–446, Figs. 1–6, Tables I–III | B3-N03 pp. 2618–2622, Figs. 1–4, Tables 1–2 | B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Group excavated volume and substrate-dependent shape. Individual pellet handling observed separately.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Adult workers excavate and move grains or pellets, with material-dependent outcomes.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No direct measurement of the uniform geometry reach, cuboid patch, assigned work duration or energy debit. Exact lookup is not a tactile sensory measurement.

CodeElement: Soil carriage, deposit, pickup and refill
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Drop releases at current location, pickup requires reachable deposited parcel and capacity. Fill requires matching held parcel, reachable no-rock void and no encased ant, food or nest anchor.
InformationChannel: Custody, carried volume and contact/geometry constraints
EvidenceLocators: B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods | B3-N05 Sections 2.2–2.6 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Pellet pickup/deposition rates by pile contact and CT-inferred refilled volumes.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Workers deposit and recover material and real nests can be remodeled.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Explicit Pickup/Fill availability is separate from the autonomous Dig/Move/Drop/Rest path. No pile mechanics or endogenous refill behavior.

CodeElement: Local excavation program and bounded return trace
CurrentRuleOrGuard: First activation requires depot. Choose reachable frontier uniformly when away and unloaded. Otherwise move through clear local face edges maximizing Manhattan distance from depot, or backtrack at path capacity. Loaded worker follows previous waypoints and drops at path origin.
InformationChannel: Uniform frontier choice, six-axis path, finite exact return trace and ordered action outcomes
EvidenceLocators: B3-N02 pp. 18616–18619, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B3-N03 pp. 2618–2622, Figs. 1–4, Tables 1–2 | B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods | B3-N07 Sections 2 and 3, Figs. 5–10
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Group shape transition and excavation activity, pellet handling and cross-species participation.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Local amplification and excavation slowdown are candidate mechanisms supported at different endpoints.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No basis for uniform frontier picks, Manhattan distance maximization, trace capacity or depot unloading policy. Physical connected void creation does not establish biological shape emergence.

CodeElement: Demand-dependent reachable free-space proxy
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Require at least two sampled contacts. Count connected sites within Manhattan reach using six face neighbors until contact count multiplied by configured empty-site target is reached.
InformationChannel: Exact connected-waypoint count conditioned on sampled neighboring ants
EvidenceLocators: B3-N01 pp. 434–446, Figs. 1–6, Tables I–III | B3-N02 pp. 18616–18619, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B3-N05 Sections 2.2–2.6 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–5 | B3-N07 Sections 2 and 3, Figs. 5–10
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Final group volume, excavation reactivation, area-perimeter transition and temperature-specific CT geometry.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Group size and available excavation space can influence collective digging. Collision-based mechanism is an analogy from a different species.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Two sampled contacts, four sites per contact and chosen Manhattan radius are not measured stimuli. Nest size and worker distribution are not independently identified by that count.

CodeElement: SDF and dirty-cache lifecycle
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Compute capped signed distances at regular quantized samples. Only overlapping existing bricks are marked dirty on material edit, and dirty samples are excluded from valid current reads.
InformationChannel: Deterministic brick sampling, cache version and invalidation
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for a derived cache.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Derived distances accelerate geometry access and do not set construction motivation.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Brick dimensions, sample offsets and halo are representation details.

CodeElement: Weather, substrate and underground microclimate
CurrentRuleOrGuard: No temperature, pore or humidity transport, rain/flood, variable particle size, soil rheology, evaporative substrate dynamics, light or endogenous seasonal physiology.
InformationChannel: No coupled weather, granular rheology, soil/air moisture or underground temperature state
EvidenceLocators: B3-N03 pp. 2618–2622, Figs. 1–4, Tables 1–2 | B3-N05 Sections 2.2–2.6 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–5 | B3-N08 pp. 535–540, Results of Experiments 1–3 | B3-P06 Sections 2.1–2.7 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–3 and Table 2 | B3-P07 Ant survey, Fig. 2 and Tables 1–3 | B3-P09 PDF pp. 5–6 and 10–11, Fig. 8
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Excavated shape by substrate, column temperature and CT, texture locomotion, cold tolerance, field occupancy and drought survival.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Substrate and environmental history influence different stages and endpoints in the measured settings.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Care metadata and a fixed dry/water mass pair are not temperature, humidity, seasonal dormancy, pore transport or substrate behavior.

CodeElement: Initial colony and individual identities
CurrentRuleOrGuard: At time zero before execution, create a LasiusNigerEngineeringFixture colony and valid living-stage ant rows. Allocate world-qualified monotonic IDs and record the starting stage, born_at and carrying capacity.
InformationChannel: Host-supplied setup at time zero with persistent identity and clearance
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for identifier registration.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: A seeded queen, egg, larva, pupa or worker is an explicit experimental initial condition.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Founding process and colony size distribution require a separately declared experimental population. Seeding must be excluded from natural birth counts.

CodeElement: Colony size and retained dead identities
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Living count changes only on seeding, funded births or death. Stage/identity history is preserved. No colony-level birth quota or death-triggered global behavior branch.
InformationChannel: Ledger-derived life status and summary count. No colony-wide reaction to queen loss.
EvidenceLocators: B3-P03 journal pp. 398–400, Methods and Results, Appendix S2 | B3-P04 Sections 2–3, Table 1 and Table S3 | B3-P08 Sections 2(c–e) and 3, Fig. 1b–c | B3-P11 Methods and Results, Figs. 2–5, Tables 1–2 | B3-P12 accepted PDF pp. 7–12, Figs. 1–5 | B3-N05 Sections 2.2–2.6 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Founding productivity, colony worker census, queenless ovary activation and winter worker survival.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Real colony trajectories depend on stage, resource regime and caste. Worker activity can continue without a queen.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Living metadata includes all live ant stages. Experimental worker census differs. No colony-level failure rule, replacement queen or worker male reproduction from queen loss.

CodeElement: Age, hazards and sex-specific lifespan
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Only measured-in-engine reserve exhaustion or external fixture death changes life state to Dead. born_at is identity history and can be used as care context metadata.
InformationChannel: Reserve depletion or explicit externally forced death
EvidenceLocators: B3-P01 pp. 19–21, Figs. 1, 3–4, Table 1 | B3-P02 Sections 2–3, Figs. 1–3 | B3-P06 Sections 2.1–2.7 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–3 and Table 2 | B3-P09 PDF pp. 5–6 and 10–11, Fig. 8 | B3-P10 Methods and Results, Figs. 1–3 | B3-P12 accepted PDF pp. 7–12, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Adult age-at-death, dietary survival, acute thermal tolerance, desiccation and overwintering outcomes.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Survival varies by age, natal stage, conditions, diet and caste in distinct assays.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No age, exposure, injury, pathogen, thermal or sex-specific hazard beyond the current reserve/fixture path. Available studies do not identify stage-specific death risks for all juveniles.

CodeElement: Finite external resource pulses
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Release componentwise min of remaining reserve and scaled pulse limits. Optional low productivity applies on odd productive spans. Continue scheduling even if the released amount is zero.
InformationChannel: Finite supplied ingredient reserve and clock-driven componentwise release
EvidenceLocators: B3-T04 pp. 560–565, Tables 1–3 | B3-P04 Sections 2–3, Table 1 and Table S3 | B3-P06 Sections 2.1–2.7 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–3 and Table 2 | B3-P11 Methods and Results, Figs. 2–5, Tables 1–2
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Artificial diet input, colony development, deprivation responsiveness and endogenous dormancy.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Resource availability and composition affect behavior and colony endpoints in the tested regimes.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Absolute-time alternating scale, fixed composition and depletion are an external treatment generator. No prey, aphid renewal or seasonal production feedback.

CodeElement: Autonomy enrollment and wake ownership
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Reject concurrent dedicated care or externally owned resolution as applicable. Mark enrollment and enqueue at the social decision interval only for adults.
InformationChannel: External configuration or funded offspring enrollment and deterministic event ownership
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for enrollment.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Enrollment installs a runtime decision, with adulthood and care ownership as execution gates.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The first scheduled wake cannot identify age, motivation or natural onset. B3-C02 concerns measured task heterogeneity.

CodeElement: Eligibility to switch daily programs
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Switch only when stationary or exactly at depot and not carrying food or soil. Ordinary workers also wait for minimum program time except paused or forced return-to-rest. Active care leases keep ordinary wake but block selection.
InformationChannel: Exact program, depot coordinates, cargo, reserve fraction and care lease
EvidenceLocators: B3-T01 pp. 214–216, 225–230, Fig. 6 | B3-T08 Sections 2.2 and 3.1–3.8, Figs. 1–3 | B3-T09 Methods, Biological material, and Results, worker groups
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Individual task observation counts, queen care scan proportions and age-by-role samples.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Behavior profiles and queen worker-dependent care are observed under specific settings.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Exact-depot switching, hard minimum dwell and no-preemption cargo gates are engineering ownership plus a switching hypothesis. No study identifies those thresholds.

CodeElement: Local worker program lottery and continuation
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Urgency plus usable stock selects Rest. Optional continuation holds Nurse if a sampled recipient can use carried nutrition. Otherwise draw weighted Rest, Forage, social Nurse, Excavate or care lease from private seed.
InformationChannel: Private weighted draw over local eligible tasks. Exact neighbor nutrient vector, nearby stock and soil are proxy channels.
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Task act distributions, scout/nestmate interactions and food-specific recruitment fractions.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Brood context, food and deprivation modulate some measured behaviors. Workers vary in observed participation.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Fixed weights, reserve quarter-cutoff, two Nurse options and numerical contact sample are not observed choices. Clock, intake and geometry alter the eligible denominator.

CodeElement: Program activation, rest and return trigger
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Cancel previously owned nutrition, foraging or excavation work and activate the selected program. Long-term return can replace wake with a next-millisecond policy wake favoring Rest.
InformationChannel: Explicit program activation, preemption, nutrition scheduler and return marker
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Observed act counts, aggregation fractions/site occupancy and qualitative dormancy.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Non-foraging and clustering have behavioral correlates that depend on setting and worker group.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Rest can invoke nutrition and basal metabolism. Nurse, Forage and Excavate may accrue active debit while waiting. Rested and program time lack a sleep or inactivity-bout definition.

CodeElement: Task age, physiological fatigue and colony division
CurrentRuleOrGuard: No explicit age-dependent transition probabilities, specialist worker morphs, individual fatigue state or social reinforcement network for allocation.
InformationChannel: No worker age, fatigue or learned propensity channel in ordinary task draw
EvidenceLocators: B3-T01 pp. 214–216, 225–230, Fig. 6 | B3-T02 Sections 2–3, Figs. 2–3, Table 1 | B3-T03 PDF pp. 2–5, Figs. 1–3 | B3-T09 Methods, Biological material, and Results, worker groups
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Marked-worker task counts, head width, group transfer latency and age-by-role molecular profiles.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Individual variation and overlap of ages/roles occur. Size association depends on endpoint and context.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No measured fatigue recovery or age-specific transition law. Private random draws and assigned caste do not implement a stable worker phenotype.

CodeElement: Absent → InitialSolid, voids, rock and soil ledger installed
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Explicit pre-seeding world setup | Valid geometry and untouched empty world | Store authority and fact. Derive exact initial Soil volume
InformationChannel: Initial geometry and host setup
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for geometry initialization.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: An explicit solid and pore arrangement establishes experimental context.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A seeded cavity is distinct from a cavity that animals chose or excavated.

CodeElement: Current ordered edits → New geometry revision
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Successful excavate or fill | Validated volume and parcel movement | Append linked edit and invalidate derived cached bricks, not historical material identity
InformationChannel: Edit revision with exact material accounting
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for versioning.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Conserved soil relocation is recorded as an edit and a parcel change.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Versioned topology records a physical model state, independent of excavation stimulus validity.

CodeElement: Current position → New spatial index / no movement
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Committed move or care movement | Continuous/legacy path and body or load clearance | Move authoritatively, update indexes and soil position, interrupt incompatible custody
InformationChannel: Swept physical envelope and contact index
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for index membership.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Legal movement updates the represented body and its custody.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Clearance cannot identify body rotations, squeezing or carrying motor trajectories.

CodeElement: Quantized start/destination → Returned candidate route / rejected or exhausted
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Public query or validation | Six face steps, bounds, geometry and route budget. Validation rechecks current edges | Produce read-only versioned route. No autonomous access to a route to unknown food.
InformationChannel: Administrative six-neighbor route query and budget
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for A*.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Query is a world-geometry diagnostic.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The returned path is not an observed internal map or forager perception.

CodeElement: Soil in reachable patch → Rejected / eligible to excavate
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Resolution after work duration | Reachable face, no rock, positive volume, loaded clearance, capacity and sufficient energy | Only eligible action debits actual soil and reserves
InformationChannel: Face reach, work clock and cargo/reserve checks
EvidenceLocators: B3-N01 pp. 434–446, Figs. 1–6, Tables I–III | B3-N03 pp. 2618–2622, Figs. 1–4, Tables 1–2
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Group digging rate and material-dependent morphology.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Real effort and excavation outcomes vary with substrate and group.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Finite patch, exact face query, loaded envelope and modeled cost are uncalibrated.

CodeElement: Soil volume in solid → ParcelState::Carried
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Successful excavation | Budgets permit edit and parcel identity | Debit solid volume and energy, establish carrier and edit fact
InformationChannel: Commit removal, cost debit and carried parcel
EvidenceLocators: B3-N03 pp. 2618–2622, Figs. 1–4, Tables 1–2 | B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Observed material removal and pellet custody.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Workers carry particles after removing substrate.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: An exact uniform cuboid does not represent the distribution of natural grains or bite effort.

CodeElement: Carried → Deposited
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Valid Drop | Actor owns matching parcel | Store current position and update carried/deposited ledgers
InformationChannel: Matching held parcel and actor position
EvidenceLocators: B3-N01 pp. 434–446, Figs. 1–6, Tables I–III | B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Excavated mass at collection site and location-dependent pellet drops.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Workers carry and deposit soil.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Core's drop-at-current-position and usual origin return ignore pile signals and changing local topography.

CodeElement: Deposited → Carried
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Valid Pickup | In contact and physically clear, no conflicting load, capacity sufficient | Commit parcel carrier, position and ledger transfer
InformationChannel: Deposited parcel contact and capacity check
EvidenceLocators: B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Pickup frequency conditional on contact and pile size.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Individual pellet pickup was observed in assembly assay.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The explicit command does not instantiate conditional worker choice or a height-based pile interaction.

CodeElement: Carried and reachable Void → Smaller carried parcel or Exhausted; Soil in patch
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Valid Fill | Enough parcel volume, no rock or embedded physical entity or anchor | Conserved fill and geometry revision. Subsequent route and care use new geometry.
InformationChannel: Reachable void, matching carrier and vacancy of patch
EvidenceLocators: B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods | B3-N05 Sections 2.2–2.6 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Pellet deposition and inferred upper-cavity refill volume.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Colony-built soil structures can be remodeled.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: CT cannot distinguish all refill microactions. A legal explicit Fill does not add an autonomous refill trigger.

CodeElement: Inactive / active → Enabled with wake / disabled
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Behavior start or interruption | Requires current path or initial depot at waypoint, death removes queued work | Activate/cancel deterministic owned wake
InformationChannel: Waypoint and scheduler ownership
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for event ownership.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The program starts or cancels one scheduler.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: First activation at an exact point and retained finite memory are implementation constraints.

CodeElement: Worker at local waypoint → Rest / Move / Excavate / Drop pending
CurrentRuleOrGuard: ExcavationWake | Load, prior path, frontier, portal and capacity gates | Local choice schedules actual soil/move/rest resolution with matching duration
InformationChannel: Frontier/load gates plus sampled local geometry
EvidenceLocators: B3-N02 pp. 18616–18619, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B3-N03 pp. 2618–2622, Figs. 1–4, Tables 1–2 | B3-N04 pp. 1303–1307, Figs. 1–3 and SI Methods | B3-N07 Sections 2 and 3, Figs. 5–10
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Excavation shape, soil handling and comparative participation.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Multiple processes can generate different local digging and transfer patterns.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Uniform reachable frontiers, pure Manhattan outward drive and trace reversal were not measured.

CodeElement: Resolved movement or soil action → Trace and counters updated / next wake
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Committed result callback | Only owned action, only real movements change path | Trim revisited path, append new waypoint, rearm
InformationChannel: Committed path and counter updates
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for trace bookkeeping.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Only a real successful move changes the stored path.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Deque/array update and repeated exact waypoints do not establish a worker's return-memory representation.

CodeElement: Locally sampled contact density → Demand false / true
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Ordinary worker policy | Configured geometry and long-term feedback, quantized actor and two or more sampled contacts | Return whether bounded connected sites are below the count threshold
InformationChannel: Sampled contacts and bounded connected sites
EvidenceLocators: B3-N01 pp. 434–446, Figs. 1–6, Tables I–III | B3-N02 pp. 18616–18619, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B3-N05 Sections 2.2–2.6 and 3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–5 | B3-N07 Sections 2 and 3, Figs. 5–10
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Colony-size/volume contrasts, shape transitions and CT remodeling.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Occupancy-related constraints and space feedback are plausible.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Group endpoints and cross-species collision model cannot identify a per-contact vacancy threshold.

CodeElement: External initial input → Egg / Larva / Pupa / Adult
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Seed call before execution | Valid caste/stage, referenced colony, world bounds and body clearance | New identity plus AntSeeded fact, contact index and living count
InformationChannel: Validated explicit stage and identity setup
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for seeding.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Registration supplies a declared assay initial condition.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A seeded late-stage ant cannot be counted as a naturally surviving egg or a new worker from the queen.

CodeElement: Registered resource / pulse pending → Reserve installed / released mass / depleted reserve
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Setup and periodic wake | One config per source, finite reserves, bounded interval and rate | Conserved ingredient debit/credit, exact fact including zero, rearm
InformationChannel: Host finite reserve and absolute clock for release
EvidenceLocators: B3-T04 pp. 560–565, Tables 1–3 | B3-P04 Sections 2–3, Table 1 and Table S3 | B3-P11 Methods and Results, Figs. 2–5, Tables 1–2
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Food-deprivation response and growth under prescribed diets.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Manipulating available resources changes colony endpoints.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Regular pulses and zero-input events describe bookkeeping. Diet schedules and natural flux are different estimands.

CodeElement: Not enrolled / disabled → Enabled with adult wake or dormant juvenile
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Explicit enable or funded birth | Alive admissible caste and physiology, social enabled and no incompatible action ownership | Record enrollment. First adult wake is after social interval.
InformationChannel: Setup eligibility plus one adult wake
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Setup is a runnable experimental actor condition.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No age-specific onset probability or juvenile task learning is observed by scheduling.

CodeElement: Enabled → Disabled
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Explicit disable | Dedicated care policy differs from integrated lease | Interrupt integrated lease, cancel policy wake and record change
InformationChannel: Host disable and care ownership
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Owned events are canceled consistently.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Manual disable is an intervention rather than a spontaneous change of motivation.

CodeElement: Enabled without wake / enabled → Active wake / disabled after death
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Adult activation / terminal life transition | Enabled adult with no existing wake / registered autonomous state | Schedule one decision or cancel and deactivate
InformationChannel: Stage and terminal queue cleanup
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The event boundary makes scheduling safe.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Emergence need not coincide with immediate mature task propensity. A cleared wake does not model mortality.

CodeElement: Traveling / loaded / in care → Current program retained
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Ordinary wake | No switching while travel away, carrying or leased care as applicable | Keep program, advance decision bookkeeping and rearm
InformationChannel: Carry status, exact depot and current lease
EvidenceLocators: B3-T01 pp. 214–216, 225–230, Fig. 6 | B3-T09 Methods, Biological material, and Results, worker groups
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Repeated task observation and bait-defined role.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Specialization and repeat activity occur in observed workers.

CodeElement: Integrated adult queen available → Care lease or current program
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Ordinary wake | Admissible location/cargo, not urgent, time since change strictly positive, local care available | Start care on selection or keep current role
InformationChannel: Local queen care availability and own reserves
EvidenceLocators: B3-T08 Sections 2.2 and 3.1–3.8, Figs. 1–3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Active brood-care fraction under worker manipulations.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Queen care changes with worker presence and may reverse after removal.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Reserve and timing guards, exact location and modeled sensory channels are additional hypotheses.

CodeElement: Worker available / depot return → Rest or Nurse continuation
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Policy wake | Return marker in long-term mode, urgent compatible depot stock, or active Nurse with exchange and compatible carried nutrients | Apply actual program change only when selection differs
InformationChannel: Return marker, stock, urgent reserve or compatible sampled need
EvidenceLocators: B3-T04 pp. 560–565, Tables 1–3 | B3-T07 pp. 116–120, Fig. 2, Table 1 | B3-T08 Sections 2.2 and 3.1–3.8, Figs. 1–3 | B3-P02 Sections 2–3, Figs. 1–3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Food-type and deprivation effects, and queen care response.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: State and social conditions can change observed response or participation.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No observed threshold or rule for forced Rest, nutrient-vector access or donation continuation.

CodeElement: Worker available → Rest / Forage / Nurse / Excavate / care lease
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Policy wake after dwell or when paused | Positive weight and task-specific local eligibility | Use actor-private weighted draw, batch choices then commit in actor order
InformationChannel: Weighted alternatives, local eligibility and actor-private randomness
EvidenceLocators: B3-T01 pp. 214–216, 225–230, Fig. 6 | B3-T02 Sections 2–3, Figs. 2–3, Table 1 | B3-T03 PDF pp. 2–5, Figs. 1–3 | B3-T07 pp. 116–120, Fig. 2, Table 1 | B3-T09 Methods, Biological material, and Results, worker groups
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Task events, body-size associations, transfer efficiency and food-response contrasts.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Behavioral choices vary across individuals, colonies and contexts.

CodeElement: Returned worker → Rest pending
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Committed return callback | Long-term config and enabled autonomy | Replace ordinary wake with return-marked wake one millisecond later
InformationChannel: Committed return and one-ms scheduling delay
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for priority rescheduling.
SupportedBiologicalClaim: This schedules next-step recovery and intake opportunities.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: One millisecond is a causality convention, with no natural post-trip latency inference.

CodeElement: Active ordinary program → Paused
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Manual pause or program preemption | Live registered physiological actor. Reject conflicting external work. | Settle to boundary and cancel owned behavioral events. Keep physiology running.
InformationChannel: Manual role control or finite care preemption

CodeElement: Available worker → Forage
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Explicit program change or committed local policy choice | Adult Worker with valid configured surface and admissible remembered or initial route | Install forager ownership and its Perception wake
InformationChannel: Admissible foraging state and scheduled local wake
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Nest exit responses and conditional scout outcomes.

CodeElement: Available worker → Excavate

InformationChannel: Worker at configured valid excavation waypoint

CurrentRuleOrGuard: Explicit program change, local policy choice or finite care lease | Living Adult Worker. Care motor suppresses the ordinary nutrition wake. | Schedule ordinary NutritionWake for Rest/Nurse or allow timed care to own the motor. Record actual role change.
